title: Discovery drill: an HR assistant request
summary: Write the questions you would ask, then compare with a model list.
scenario: The head of HR at a multinational says: 'We want an AI chatbot for HR.' You have a first meeting and two weeks for discovery. Constructed for teaching.

categories.name: Outcome
categories.hint: What problem and what measurable result?

categories.name: Process
categories.hint: How is it done today and where does it hurt?

categories.name: Data
categories.hint: Where is the information and who owns it?

categories.name: Risk and compliance
categories.hint: What is the cost of a wrong answer? Which rules apply?

categories.name: Users
categories.hint: Who will use it and how?

categories.name: Constraints
categories.hint: Budget, time, platforms, skills, data location

categories.name: Success metrics
categories.hint: How will we know it worked?

model_questions.question: Which HR tasks or queries do you most want to improve, and what would a good result look like in numbers?
Who benefits most: employees, HR staff, managers?
Can you show me the last ten real employee queries and how each was handled?
Where do delays and errors occur today, and how many queries arrive per week by type?
Which documents and systems hold the answers, who owns them and how current are they?
Which of those contain personal or sensitive data, and what are we allowed to use them for?
What is the worst consequence of a wrong answer in each query type, and who would be accountable?
Which countries and employee groups are in scope, and what privacy or works-council rules apply?
How do employees ask for help today and what do they trust or distrust about it?
What platforms, identity systems and security standards must we use, and what budget and timeline apply?
What is the baseline for handling time and satisfaction, and what improvement would justify the investment?
How will we collect the measures after launch, and who reviews them?
